title: Brightening serum for post-acne hyperpigmentation in Fitzpatrick IV to VI: a planned open-label study at an academic centre, brand collaborator
headline: A 20-person, open-label, single-centre study of a French cosmetic brightening serum for post-acne dark marks in medium to deep skin is registered to start in Sept 2026; no results, no control arm, and the brand is a collaborator.
evidenceTier: Trial registry record, read in full; no results
fit: Pigment-prone skin: Partial. Right population (Fitzpatrick IV to VI); weak design. The formula has no acid, retinoid or niacinamide, so it would layer easily with those.
displaces: Would replace an existing brightening serum step, not add one.
regions: Global (cosmetic; the registry record names the brand Caudalie as collaborator)
estimateNote: Prices marked EST are my guesses, not looked up.
buzzCheck: Priced like a premium serum. Evidence is brand claims plus a registered 20-person open-label study with no results, so the price does not track evidence yet.
summaryPoints: Observation (registry record read): Weill Cornell Medicine, New York; n=20 planned; adults with Fitzpatrick IV to VI, moderate to severe post-acne PIH (PAHPI score 8 or more), mild acne only; 12 weeks; primary outcome is change in PAHPI at week 12; secondary outcomes are tolerability and a patient-reported stigma questionnaire.
Observation: status not yet recruiting; start Sept 2026; primary completion 15 Jan 2027. Participants must use no other facial products during the study.

Observation (registry): the product is described only as 'Vinoperfect brightening serum' with Caudalie as collaborator. Update 2026-11-16: I opened the brand and retailer pages for the Caudalie Vinoperfect Brightening Dark Spot Serum (sold in Canada as the Radiance Serum, Vitamin C alternative). Inference: this is probably the trial product, but the registry does not say so.
Limits: no comparator; the brand is a collaborator; 20 people.

Observation (brand page, Canada, read 2026-11-16): full ingredient list begins water, butylene glycol, glycerin, coco-caprylate/caprate, squalane, palmitoyl grapevine shoot extract (the marketed 'viniferine'), then emulsifiers, bisabolol, preservatives and fragrance. No concentration is stated for any ingredient. It contains no niacinamide, acid or retinoid.

Observation (brand claims, not independent evidence): the page cites 62 times the effect of vitamin C in a lab tyrosinase test, 43% better than 10% niacinamide in an ex vivo test, a 63% reduction after one bottle (65 volunteers, 56 days) and 81% on deeper skin tones (33 volunteers). No papers are linked for these.

Price: 30 ml about 110 on the Caudalie Canada page and 110 on the Sephora Canada page, checked 2026-11-16 (the pages do not label the currency; both are Canadian storefronts). 50 ml size also sold; price not captured.
toneData: Fitzpatrick IV to VI by protocol, any ethnicity
fitLine: Population is relevant; a small open-label brand-linked study will tell me little about whether the serum beats a plain moisturizer plus sunscreen.

fitAxes.why: The protocol asks participants to avoid sun and use sun protection as part of the routine.
